description:
Ice Cream Stabilizers: Xanthan Gum is the first video about a single stabiliser.

First off, excuse the naff setting for the video as we are in an AirBnB and not here for very long. Also, all my stuff is currently on a big ship sailing across the Atlantic. 

Xanthan gum is a great stand alone start to using stabilizers in your ice cream, it's really easy to use, hydrates in cold liquids and produces a decent result. As time goes on, your realise there are much better combos though so stay tuned and don't forget to like and subscribe. 

There is a great scientific website on Xanthan gum should you want to have some "Easy Reading", check the link https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/xanthan-gum

-----------------------

If you want to watch me use Xanthan gum in a recipe, check out this video:
https://youtu.be/zRbNJEJ5hrg

----------------------

If you want to see me talk about Rocky Road's history, check out this video:
https://youtu.be/9KscR8IN56Q

----------------------

If you enjoyed this video, please consider liking, commenting and subscribing, plus pop over to our Instagram page linked below and say hello :)

Instagram: https://tinyurl.com/2p85zcxh
Facebook: Don't use it anymore, sorry but feel free to like etc  
Website: https://www.polaricecreamery.com
Ko-Fi Link: https://ko-fi.com/icecreamery


Thanks and see you on the next video :)

Interesting, what you said about not adding it to a hot mix. What do you consider too hot?
I use a combo of CMC and Xanthan for sorbets and I always heat up the water to around 65 to ensure proper hydration of all the powders. But maybe that's not necessary? comments.text:
Both CMC and Xanthan are cold hydrating powders. You can add them to 10g of sugar and mix in to a cold liquid. No need to heat at all.
I’d say your numbers are off if you’re getting a foam texture in the churn.

comments.text: @babakk.8166  yeah the aging process is about the infusion of flavour and settling of fat and protein. The composition of milk and cream will dictate the stabilizer but are you using inulin as the only “sugar” source?

comments.text:
This is basically for a lime sorbet I'm trying to perfect. I've worked on it for quite a while to get a decent "creamy" texture and as close to the Italian standards as possible. I'm using sugar, dextrose, and dry glucose DE42, and the stabilizers mentioned above. It wasn't great until I added Inulin which I guess is helping to add body, being a fiber. I just haven't figured out that foam feeling on the tongue when it comes out of the machine (at about -6). I wonder if using cool water will help. Or maybe less Inulin cause I've heard it can make it stretchy or stringy.
Looking forward or more stabilizer videos :)
comments.author: @babakk.8166

comments.text: @babakk.8166  honestly....I think you are over complicating the recipe for a sorbet. I've made dozens since my raspberry sorbet and all of them have been super simple and the results are amazing. Only yesterday did I have a sorbet from a local shop which is highly recommended, their sorbet was the same as mine. You're using 3 sugars + inulin and I would just use pectin. I don't know your full recipe so am only guessing but id say the inulin + stabilizers etc are whipping your base.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
Oh I know, it's complicated indeed haha I've spent a year and over 50 test batches to get to a very specific texture with this. I'm a perfectionist. It's been my most complicated flavour because it's all liquid with no fruit fiber to help. Mind you that this is for a potential future business of mine so no cutting corners. I'm looking for that premium mouth feel.

I spent most of my life passionately hating all sorbets around here (Montreal) and probably most north america, thinking it just wasn't for me. Too sweet, too sour, too gloopy, slow flavour release, too stretchy. All that until I started to travel. Now I know I can enjoy a sorbet that has a nice balance, that melts quickly on the tongue to release the flavour, and feels thin.
My weakest point is fully understanding the function of each stabilizer and little details that may or may not make a big difference. And the quantity of course. I started with Pregel but I'm over them. It's all from scratch now.
Most Italian videos out there talk forever with close to zero useful information.
Pectin texture didn't do it for me. My 3 sugars is mostly to reduce the high sweetness level that North American sorbet offer. But I'm still experimenting with quantities. 
See you on the next stabilizer video.
comments.author: @babakk.8166

comments.text: @babakk.8166  ah yes I know that feeling. Well, I’ve got lots of stabilizer videos coming up to keep you going and if I can help in any way, just let me know.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery
